meta.name: Microsoft Power Automate RPA Developer Associate (PL-500)
meta.notes: Initial pack — 12 scenario-style questions across the four PL-500 domains: designing automations, developing automations (desktop + cloud flows), deploying and managing the solution (machines, machine groups, ALM), and process advisor / AI Builder integration.

questions.question: A team wants to record how staff move data between SAP, Excel and a legacy WinForms app on their own desktops over two weeks, then have Power Automate suggest which steps can be automated. Which Power Platform capability fits this scenario?
options: A Power BI dashboard pointed at the activity logs in Microsoft 365 audit logs
Process advisor's task mining, which records desktop activity and clusters it into a recommended automation
An attended desktop flow that runs as each user signs in and writes telemetry to Dataverse
A Power Automate cloud flow using the 'When an activity occurs' trigger on Office 365 audit logs
questions.explanation: Process advisor has two modes — process mining (analyses event logs from an existing system) and task mining (records the user's desktop activity and clusters the recorded steps into tasks and variants). Task mining is what you reach for when you want to capture cross-application desktop work and surface automation candidates. M365 audit logs do not capture per-keystroke desktop activity, an attended desktop flow only runs the automation rather than analysing usage, and there is no audit-log trigger that captures local-app interactions inside SAP or a WinForms app.

questions.question: A bot must log into a vendor portal in Edge, download a CSV file, and email it to finance. It must run overnight on a server with no user signed in, and may run on many servers in parallel as volume grows. Which Power Automate object should be built?
options: An attended desktop flow triggered by a 'Schedule cloud flow' that opens Edge interactively in the user's session
A Power Fx canvas app that opens the portal in an embedded web control during the night
A cloud flow only, using the HTTP action to scrape the portal — desktop flows are not designed for browser automation
An unattended desktop flow distributed across a machine group, started from a scheduled cloud flow
questions.explanation: Unattended desktop flows run on a Windows machine with no interactive user signed in — they sign in to a dedicated Windows account themselves and execute the recorded UI steps. Distributing them through a machine group lets Power Automate pick an available machine each run, which is the standard way to scale out volume. Attended flows require a user to be at the desktop, the cloud-flow HTTP action will not work against an authenticated portal that has no API, and a canvas app is a user-facing application, not a scheduled background bot.

questions.question: A desktop flow clicks an OK button on a vendor application. After a vendor update the layout shifts and the recorded selector no longer matches, even though the button still says 'OK' and still has the same control name in the UI tree. Which adjustment makes the selector most resilient?
options: Switch the action to use image-based recognition so it matches the button by visual appearance
Increase the global timeout so Power Automate Desktop waits longer before failing
Edit the UI element selector to remove fragile attributes that changed and keep the stable ones (e.g. control Name, ClassName) — using the custom selector builder
Re-record the entire flow from scratch so a new selector is captured
questions.explanation: The recommended approach in Power Automate Desktop when a selector breaks is to open the UI element in the selector builder and trim or tweak attributes — keep the stable ones (control name, class, role) and remove the fragile ones (window title that changed, position-in-tree indexes). Image-based recognition is a last resort because it is brittle to theming, DPI and screen resolution. Increasing the timeout does not help if the selector is wrong. Re-recording is wasteful when a one-line selector fix would do — and it loses any custom logic around the action.

questions.question: Inside a Power Automate desktop flow, several actions need to retry on failure and a clean-up action must always run even if every retry exhausts. Which construct should the developer add?
options: Wrap the actions in an 'On block error' block configured with a retry policy, and put the clean-up actions after the block so they always run
Wrap the actions in a 'Loop' with a counter and put the clean-up inside the loop body
Set the global flow retry policy in the desktop flow properties so all actions in the flow retry automatically
Move the work into a subflow and call it from a 'Run desktop flow' action with the Continue on error setting enabled
questions.explanation: Power Automate Desktop provides a dedicated 'On block error' action that wraps a group of actions, lets you set how many times the block retries and the delay between retries, and lets you decide whether to continue, throw, or set a variable when the block ultimately fails. Placing the clean-up actions after the block (or inside a Finally-style branch) guarantees they run after retries are exhausted. There is no flow-wide retry policy setting, a plain Loop has no built-in retry semantics, and Continue on error on an action only suppresses errors — it does not retry.

questions.question: A cloud flow calls a desktop flow that returns a list of invoice numbers. In the desktop flow, how is that list of values surfaced so the cloud flow can iterate over each invoice in an Apply to each?
options: Save the values to a CSV file on disk and let the cloud flow read the file with the File System connector
Concatenate the values into a single string and parse it in the cloud flow with the Split function
Write the values to a Dataverse table inside the desktop flow and query Dataverse from the cloud flow
Mark the desktop-flow variables as Output (External) variables — they appear as dynamic content in the cloud flow's 'Run a flow built with Power Automate Desktop' action
questions.explanation: Desktop-flow variables can be flagged as Input (External) or Output (External). Output variables appear as dynamic content on the cloud flow action that invokes the desktop flow, so a list variable comes through as an array that an Apply to each can loop over natively. Writing to disk, Dataverse, or a concatenated string all work but are unnecessary indirection — the supported, supported, and supported-everywhere mechanism is the External output variable on the desktop flow itself.

questions.question: An organisation wants Power Automate Desktop bots to run on Azure-hosted Windows machines provisioned and patched by Microsoft, with no on-premises infrastructure. Which Power Automate feature should be chosen?
options: An on-premises data gateway in standard mode pointing at a Hyper-V VM
Hosted machines (and hosted machine groups), which provision cloud Windows VMs managed by Microsoft for unattended automation
Customer-managed Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts connected to Power Automate over the on-premises data gateway
An attended desktop flow distributed via Intune to user laptops
questions.explanation: Hosted machines and hosted machine groups are the Power Automate feature that gives you Microsoft-managed cloud Windows VMs for running unattended desktop flows — no Azure subscription, gateway or VM provisioning of your own. The on-premises data gateway only proxies traffic into customer-managed environments. Customer-managed AVD with a gateway is a valid topology but it is not Microsoft-managed and requires the customer to operate the VMs. Attended flows on user laptops do not run unattended overnight.

questions.question: An RPA solution (cloud flow + desktop flow + connection references + environment variables) has to move cleanly from Dev to Test to Production with admin approval, and admins want a guarantee that no one can edit it directly in Production. Which approach satisfies all three goals?
options: Use Power Platform Pipelines (or the equivalent ALM Accelerator) to deploy a managed solution from Dev → Test → Prod, with approvals configured between stages
Export the components as unmanaged solutions from Dev and re-import them as unmanaged into Test and Production for easy hotfixing
Share the flows with the production users directly from Dev so they pick up the live version without a deployment
Copy and paste the flow XML into each environment via the Power Automate maker portal
questions.explanation: The recommended ALM path for Power Platform — flows, connection references, environment variables, custom connectors, Dataverse customisations — is a managed solution promoted with Power Platform Pipelines (or ALM Accelerator) from Dev to Test to Prod with approvals. Managed solutions in Production cannot be customised in place, which gives the immutability guarantee. Unmanaged solutions are intended for the development environment only; sharing across environments is not deployment; and pasting XML is not a supported deployment mechanism.

questions.question: A bot logs into a vendor portal whose username and password are rotated every 30 days. Where should those credentials live so the desktop flow uses the latest secret without being edited each rotation, and so security can audit access?
options: Hard-code the credentials in a 'Set variable' action at the top of the flow and update them on rotation
Save them to a plain-text file on the bot machine that the flow reads at the start
Store them in an Azure Key Vault secret and reference the secret via an environment variable of type 'Secret' (backed by Key Vault) used by the flow
Email the credentials to a shared mailbox and parse them from the latest message at runtime
questions.explanation: Power Platform environment variables support a 'Secret' data type that is backed by Azure Key Vault. The solution stores a reference to the secret (not the secret itself), and the flow resolves the current value at runtime — rotating the secret in Key Vault means no edit to the flow, and Key Vault provides the audit trail. Hard-coded variables and plain-text files leak credentials and force edits on rotation; mining a shared mailbox at runtime is fragile and not auditable.

questions.question: A cloud flow needs to extract the supplier name, invoice number and total from PDF invoices uploaded to a SharePoint library, without anyone writing regex against the raw text. Which approach is the canonical Power Automate fit?
options: An AI Builder 'Extract information from invoices' (invoice processing) action, called from the cloud flow with the PDF as input
A desktop flow that opens each PDF in Adobe Reader and copy-pastes the text into Excel
A custom connector that posts the PDF bytes to a public OCR website
A Power Automate expression using substring() and indexOf() on the file content returned by SharePoint
questions.explanation: AI Builder ships a prebuilt 'Invoice processing' model and corresponding 'Extract information from invoices' action that returns structured fields (supplier, invoice number, totals, line items) from PDF or image invoices — this is the canonical Power Automate fit. Driving Acrobat from a desktop flow is brittle, sending documents to an unmanaged public site has obvious data-governance issues, and parsing PDF bytes by hand with string expressions ignores text encoding and layout.

questions.question: An attended desktop flow that processes customer records is failing intermittently because Power Automate Desktop cannot find a button until the page has fully rendered. The developer wants a clean fix that does not add fixed Wait actions throughout the flow. What is the recommended action?
options: Add a fixed 'Wait' action of 30 seconds before every UI step so the page is always ready
Refresh the browser before each UI action with Ctrl+F5
Turn the action's 'Continue on error' option on so the flow does not stop when the click misses
Use a 'Wait for window content' or 'Wait for image / UI element' action that blocks only until the element actually appears, with a timeout
questions.explanation: Power Automate Desktop has dedicated synchronisation actions — Wait for window content, Wait for image, Wait for UI element — that block until the condition is true (or a timeout expires). They are the right replacement for fixed Wait actions: faster on a fast machine, reliable on a slow one. Fixed Waits everywhere make the flow slow and still unreliable; Continue on error hides failure instead of fixing it; reloading the page resets context and slows everything down.

questions.question: Several desktop flows share an identical 12-step routine that signs into an internal ticketing system. The team wants one place to maintain that routine and call it from every flow. Which Power Automate Desktop feature is intended for this?
options: Copy and paste the 12 steps into each flow and rely on Git to keep them in sync
Create a subflow in each flow with the routine, and remember to update every flow when the routine changes
Build the routine once as a subflow inside a single 'shared' desktop flow and call it from the other flows using the 'Run desktop flow' action
Move the routine into a Power Automate cloud flow and start a cloud flow from the desktop flow whenever sign-in is needed
questions.explanation: Subflows live inside a single desktop flow and only that flow can call them. The supported way to share a routine across multiple desktop flows is to put it in its own desktop flow and call it with the 'Run desktop flow' action, passing inputs and reading outputs through External variables. Copy/paste does not centralise maintenance, per-flow subflows still duplicate the code, and round-tripping into a cloud flow for a local UI routine is the wrong layer.

questions.question: Many makers across an organisation are building their own desktop flows, and the centre of excellence wants visibility on which connectors and which premium features are in use, plus the ability to enforce DLP across environments. Which Power Platform tool should the CoE start with?
options: Power BI Desktop pointed at the maker portal exports refreshed nightly
The CoE Starter Kit, combined with the Power Platform admin centre's DLP policies and environment management
The Process advisor task-mining recorder running on every maker's machine
A SharePoint list where makers self-report what they have built
questions.explanation: The Microsoft-published CoE Starter Kit is the canonical accelerator for tenant-wide visibility (inventory of flows, apps, connectors, makers, usage), and DLP policies plus environment management in the Power Platform admin centre are the governance levers for restricting which connectors can be combined. Power BI exports of the maker portal do not exist as a turnkey artefact, task mining records desktop activity rather than tenant inventory, and a self-reporting SharePoint list does not actually enforce or measure anything.
